newsitem.title: CHINA: China to cut red tape for Taiwan reporters.
newsitem.headline: China to cut red tape for Taiwan reporters.

text.p: China has issued new regulations aimed at cutting red tape for reporters from island rival Taiwan who want to cover news on the mainland, the Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.

Under the new regulations, to take effect on January 1, 1997, Taiwanese journalists covering news in China may directly apply 10 days in advance to the Taiwan Affairs Office of the State Council or local offices authorised by the State Council, Xinhua said.

Reporters from the island, which Beijing considers a rebel province, must now route their applications through the Hong Kong office of Xinhua, China's unofficial embassy in the British colony. Applications have to be made 15 days in advance.

The rules, issued on Sunday by the State Council's Taiwan Affairs Office, would still limit Taiwanese reporters to stays of one month, Xinhua said. China has not allowed the island's journalists to be based on the mainland.
Taiwanese reporters should not report rumours or use "improper means" to gather news, Xinhua said, warning of punishment in the case of legal violations.
China and Taiwan have been arch-rivals since the two were separated at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
